subject: APAC & EU data residency constraints — fallback and routing playbook
messages:
From: Sofie Bergstrom <sofie.bergstrom@neobank-eu.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procure@neobank-eu.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Jan 2026 18:12:00 +0100
Subject: RFP follow-up: data residency / APAC constraints

Hi Markus,

Thanks for the overview during the demo earlier. As part of our RFP technical annex we need concise, machine-readable answers on a couple of data residency scenarios for NeoBank's international footprint: EU primary storage, failover to APAC (Singapore/Tokyo), and a US-hosted fallback only if APAC capacity is unavailable.

Specifically:
- Can Redwood pin customer data and inference workloads to the EU (Frankfurt/Paris) with egress blocked to outside EU by default?
- If we enable APAC failover, can we restrict the APAC fallback to specific regions (e.g., ap-northeast-1 only) and prevent automatic routing to other APAC zones?
- What controls exist to prevent failover to the US unless explicitly allowed, and how quickly can we revert routing if capacity unexpectedly shifts?
- For on-prem/private deployment customers, what is the recommended approach to keep logs/audit trails within a region?

We are consolidating answers from vendors on Monday and would appreciate a short, precise matrix we can include in the annex. Attachments are fine (PDF preferred).

Cheers,
Sofie
Sofie Bergstrom
Head of Platform Risk — NeoBank EU

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Sofie Bergstrom <sofie.bergstrom@neobank-eu.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procure@neobank-eu.com>
Date: Sat, 11 Jan 2026 08:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: RFP follow-up: data residency / APAC constraints

Hi Sofie —

Thanks for the clear list. I attached a short playbook (redwood-data-map-2026.pdf) and a routing table that maps our default policies. High-level answers below; I can break these into a matrix layout if you prefer.

1) EU pinning and egress controls: Yes. For hosted accounts we support region pinning (customer primary region = eu-central-1 or eu-west-3). By default we do not route inference or store model artifacts outside the pinned region unless an explicit routing policy is set. Egress controls are implemented via tenant-level routing policies + VPC peering constraints for Private deployments.

2) APAC failover scoping: You can define an ordered list of APAC regions as acceptable failovers (e.g., ap-northeast-1, ap-southeast-1). Failover only occurs to regions listed in your policy. Policy is enforced at the routing gateway and in the control plane — we do not auto-broadcast to all APAC zones.

3) US fallback prevention: We offer explicit allow-lists for fallback regions. If US fallback is not in the allow-list, routing will not fail to US. In addition, you can set a mandatory approval window (manual or via webhook) before any cross-region failover that would include the US. Reversion: automated rollback can be configured (default 30m) or immediate manual revert via Console/API.

4) On-prem / Private: For Private/VPC installs, logs and audit events are optionally shipped to customer-managed S3/KMS/HSM within the pinned region. We provide local-only audit collectors for air-gapped installs; we do not mirror logs outside the customer's chosen storage unless explicitly configured.

I'll loop in Karthik (service reliability) and Laura (legal/compliance) for the low-level encryption and SLA notes you might want in the annex.

Best,
Markus Klein
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-data-map-2026.pdf (pdf), apac-region-routing-table.xlsx (xlsx)

Karthik/Laura — forwarding Sofie's RFP questions (NeoBank EU). Can you please confirm the technical detail for the annex: KMS residency guarantees, cross-region replication window, and the concrete controls for preventing US fallback? I proposed the manual-approval webhook option as an extra control, but want SR/Compliance signoff on wording.

Key asks:
- Can we state "audit logs are stored in customer-managed storage within pinned region" for Private and Dedicated?
- For hosted accounts, what is our documented RTO for control-plane rollback of a region-policy change?
- Any caveats around model caching/KV cache warmup that could temporarily keep tokens outside the pinned region?

Thanks — Markus

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 13 Jan 2026 11:47:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: FW: RFP follow-up: data residency / APAC constraints

Markus —

Quick technical confirmation for the RFP annex:

- KMS & encryption: For Hosted customers we integrate with regional KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS) per region and support customer-managed keys (CMKs) via external key references. For Dedicated/Private we support HSM and customer KMS endpoints. Statement: "Keys and ciphertext never leave the chosen region when using regional CMKs/HSM." (note: metadata about requests may transit control plane services — see caveat).

- Cross-region replication and cache behavior: We do not replicate persistent customer data (model weights, stored embeddings) outside pinned region unless replication is enabled by policy. KV cache used for active sequences is ephemeral; it is kept on the serving node. If a failover occurs to an approved region, warmed caches may exist in that region for short-term performance — we recommend listing this caveat in the annex.

- Control-plane rollback / RTO: For policy changes invoked via Console/API, control-plane propagation is typically under 60s for routing policy updates; enforcement at the serving layer may take up to 5 minutes to drain in-flight sessions depending on active requests. For manual immediate revert we can expedite via emergency route flush (SLA: 15 minutes for committed enterprise accounts).

- Preventing US fallback: We enforce allow-lists at the routing gateway and require either: (a) explicit allow-list entry, or (b) webhook/manual approval in the event of exhaustion. Automated fallback to an unlisted region will not occur.

I'll let Laura add legal phrasing/caveats for audit/log metadata and any statements about regulatory compliance.

—Karthik

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Sofie Bergstrom <sofie.bergstrom@neobank-eu.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Jan 2026 14:02:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: RFP follow-up: data residency / APAC constraints

Sofie —

Following Markus and Karthik's notes, a concise summary you can include in the annex:

1) Residency guarantees (hosted):
- Customer primary region can be pinned to EU (eu-central-1 or eu-west-3).
- No persistent customer data is mirrored outside the pinned region unless replication policy is enabled by the customer.

2) Failover policy and scoping:
- Customers provide an explicit ordered list of acceptable failover regions. Failover will only target regions on that list.
- US regions will never be targeted unless explicitly listed. Customers may require manual approval (webhook) before any cross-jurisdiction failover.

3) Logs, audit, and control plane: 
- For Private/Dedicated customers we support customer-managed storage and KMS within the pinned region.
- For hosted customers we provide regional KMS integration and the option to export logs to customer endpoints within the region.

4) Caveats & recommended language: 
- Ephemeral serving caches may exist in the failover region for short durations; include this sentence: "Active in-memory caches may be created in a permitted failover region to preserve session continuity; these are ephemeral and not persisted to long-term storage."
- Control-plane metadata (routing decisions, heartbeat logs) may flow through our control plane services; we recommend a line: "Control-plane metadata required for routing decisions may transit Redwood control plane services; sensitive customer payloads and persisted data remain in pinned regions when policies forbid egress."

If this looks good, Markus can upload the final RFP annex as a PDF. Happy to sign off on the language and provide a short cover note for procurement.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Head of Legal & Compliance — Redwood Inference

P.S. Markus — attaching the RFI summary doc and the regional routing table to the thread now for your outbound to NeoBank.
